figures.finding: A resident pays personal income tax (NDFL) on the main tax bases at 13% to RUB 2.4 million a year, 15% to 5 million, 18% to 20 million, 20% to 50 million and 22% above (art. 224 NK RF); there is no regional income tax.
figures.applies: Russian tax residents; tax period the calendar year 2026.

figures.finding: A Russian organisation or entrepreneur paying a person must compute, withhold and pay the NDFL, taking it from the income when actually paid (art. 226).

figures.finding: From 2023 the employer pays a single insurance contribution of 30% on pay up to the single annual base limit and 15.1% above it (art. 425); a self-employed person on the professional income tax (NPD) pays 4% on income from individuals and 6% on income from businesses and companies, with no insurance contributions, while income stays within RUB 2.4 million a year.
figures.applies: Payments to employees and contractors in Russia.

figures.finding: A non-resident pays a flat 30% on all Russian-source income, a performer's or writer's fee included (art. 224(3)), withheld by the Russian payer.
figures.applies: Individuals who are not Russian tax residents.

figures.finding: An author or performer paid royalties (for creating or performing literary and artistic works) may deduct documented expenses or, without documents, a set share of the fee: 20% for literary works (theatre and film writing included), 30% for audiovisual works (films, television), 20% for performing literary and artistic works, 40% for film and theatre design and for film music.
figures.applies: Residents receiving author's fees (art. 221(3) NK RF); claimed through the tax agent or the return.
